rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reader who cannot resolve a pronoun/demonstrative/definite noun mid-deck loses the thread. Chunk 0's pre-slide lede was cut 2026-08-25 (backing block: "re-anchored... when the pre-slide preamble was cut"), so chunk 1 now opens cold with 'the judge is miscalibrated, the gate got gamed' (line 6) -- the closest candidate to a Never-Named violation, since no prior text in this file names a judge. Checked the module-arc-beats-in-openers/closers carve-out directly against the sibling files rather than trusting the maintainer block: `grep -n '^\[' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` shows this lecture (line 56) is included immediately after `[Lecture: What packaging is]` (line 54), which follows `[Exercise: Diagnose and re-send]` (line 50); `grep -n '\bjudge\b' curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` line 74 has the student building/choosing 'a judge' as a verifier shape, and `curriculum/lectures/what-packaging-is.md:63` states this file 'is expanded by a whole lecture' for that shape. The referent is the student's just-built artefact, not a missing slide -- carve-out applies, grounded in the actual sibling text, not assumed. Rest of the sequential pass: 'the check' (line 6, second sentence) resolves within the same bullet against 'a gate' from the first sentence; 'these'/'The three countermoves' (lines 8-9) resolve against the list two clauses earlier in the same bullet; 'this loop' (line 15) and 'this'/'tampering' (line 34) are cataphoric, resolved by the colon that immediately follows in the same sentence; 'the model'/'the gates' (line 45) and 'your gates and workflow' (line 47) continue arc-earned vocabulary from lines 6-23. Harm absent throughout.

Harm: a header the chunk's own content contradicts. Closest candidate is chunk 2's third bullet (line 16, 'A good gate starts from real traces, not imagined failures...') under the header 'The judge needs calibrating against your own judgement' -- it shifts from comparing verdicts to your own review (line 14) toward how the gate itself gets built from real failure data, but it stays inside because error-analysis-first is the source of the 'own judgement' the header names: you cannot calibrate against judgements you never formed, and forming them from real traces rather than imagined ones is the same practice one step upstream. Every other header (Passing is not proof / Gates decay / One session is a sample / Change on recurrence / The delegation frontier) is a direct label of its own bullets. Harm absent.

(b) Anaphora/epistrophe triples: manual scan of all bullet-opening words, max consecutive repeat is 2 ('The check'/'The same' in adjacent clauses of line 7, not sentence-openers), no triple found; `grep -nE 'Every [a-zA-Z]+ [a-z]+ed'` -> 0 hits. (c) Self-grading superlatives (value-prop leak): `grep -niE 'one of the (most|best)|most (useful|valuable|important) (move|thing|part)'` -> 0 hits. (d) Number + own retraction: the only number in the body is line 15's '90% agreement after three iterations', stated once and never walked back; `grep -niE 'could be (more|less)|roughly|about [0-9]'` -> 0 hits, so no retraction pattern exists to trip this sub-item. (f) Verb triplets with an empty leg: `grep -nE '\bIt [a-z]+s?\. *It [a-z]+s?\. *It [a-z]+s?\.'` -> 0 hits. Harm absent on every sub-item.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a lecture header reading as a bare label/instruction where the room needs a landed claim. All six `##` headers checked: 'Passing is not proof', 'The judge needs calibrating against your own judgement', 'Gates decay', 'One session is a sample' are direct declarative claims. 'Change on recurrence, not on noise' is the closest candidate to an imperative reading -- but parses as an elliptical claim ('[The] change [happens] on recurrence, not on noise'), parallel in construction to 'Gates decay' ('[The] gates [do] decay'), and the maintainer block itself files it among the deck's five named laws ('don't-tamper (change on recurrence)'), not as an instruction to the reader. 'The delegation frontier' is a catalogue entry naming its subject, matching this rule's own cleared examples ('Ralph', 'The numbers') -- explicit not-a-violation. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a bullet that reads as rigour but adds nothing beyond what the slide already holds. Build it, then hold it to the same bar it holds the work to.', restating the H1), was already cut 2026-08-25 per the maintainer block's own dated note citing this exact rule ('check_slides.md §16 class c'); confirmed absent from the current body -- `grep -n 'one more claim in the system'` over the body -> exit 1, zero hits. Checked the remaining body for fresh instances of all three classes: (a) doctrine restatement -- no law or lens is re-announced after already doing its work; each of the five laws states once. (b) self-referential design commentary -- no line tells the student they are inside a pedagogy; body stays first-order about gates, judges and delegation throughout. (c) aphorism kicker -- checked every chunk's final bullet: line 9 (independence unifier) and line 47 (bitter lesson) are the two candidates that could read as closers, but both introduce genuinely new content beyond their header (independence as the property unifying law 1's three countermoves; model-obsolescence as a second, harder constraint on the frontier) rather than restating it, so neither is a koan. Harm absent; the maintainer-documented cut is the sole prior violation and it does not recur.
